name: Commodore Plus/4
description: A 1984 Commodore home computer aimed at home office use, with four productivity programs built into ROM. Its TED chip handled video and sound with a 121-colour palette, but it had no sprites and could not run C64 software. It sold poorly and was soon discontinued.
curiosities: Its name comes from the four built-in applications: word processor, spreadsheet, database and graphing.
It is not compatible with Commodore 64 software, despite coming out two years later.
Its datasette and joystick ports use different connectors from the C64's, so C64 peripherals needed adapters.
It shares the TED chip with the cheaper Commodore 16 and 116.
